title: Cain and Abel
english: God had regard for Abel and his offerings, but for Cain and his offerings He had no regard. Cain was very upset, and his face fell. The Lord God said to Cain, 'Why are you so deeply distressed, and why has your face fallen? If you do well, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door, and its desire is for you, but you must master it' (Genesis 4:6-7). After a while, Cain said to his brother Abel, 'Let us go out into the field' (Genesis 4:8). While they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him (Genesis 4:8). The Lord God said to Cain, 'Where is Abel, your brother?' (Genesis 4:9). But he said, 'I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?' (Genesis 4:9). And God said, 'What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground' (Genesis 4:10). Now you are cursed upon the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand. Because you work the ground, it will no longer yield its strength to you; you shall be a restless wanderer on the earth (Genesis 4:12). Cain said to the Lord, 'My punishment is too great to bear' (Genesis 4:13). And if you drive me out today from the face of the earth, and from your face I will be hidden, and I will be a wanderer and a trembler on the earth, it will happen that everyone who finds me will kill me (Genesis 4:14). But the Lord said to him, 'Not so; if anyone kills Cain, sevenfold vengeance shall be taken upon him' (Genesis 4:15). And the Lord put a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him (Genesis 4:15). So Cain went out from the presence of God.

Cain and Abel were both born from Adam, and they were like luxuriant and blooming shoots, sprouting from the roots in the beginning; human nature was concerned with fruit-bearing and growth, which was barely visible at the start and was in its early stages, but then they grew in strength. Cain preceded Abel in time of birth; Abel was also with him. They were innocent and young, like newborns nourished by their parents. When the young men reached adulthood, they turned to different pursuits. Cain, having perceived the earth's fertility and seeing it to be very abundant and most excellent, and decorated with beautiful fruits, thought that he should show his gratitude through offerings that were more pleasing to the eye than those of others; and since his household and his natural resources were working toward this automatically, as it was likely he might easily achieve a good appearance through agricultural skill, he prepared himself in a rustic manner, using all his strength, and...

title: Redemption and the Nature of Sin
english: The human condition, having been handed over to sin and entangled in the snares of death, is proclaimed beforehand to be carried to something better through the mystery of redemption.
This is made possible by Christ, who dies for us and on our behalf at the right time.
According to the faith of the holy Scriptures, the forefather Adam was created in the image and likeness of God.
From him, Cain and Abel were born.
However, Cain is assigned the face of Israel, as Christ himself considered the crowds of the Jews to be similar to Cain.
Christ's words, 'If you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free,' are a promise of freedom (John 8:31-32).
But those who did not understand the beauty of paternal freedom tried to boast in fleshly arrogance, claiming to be the seed of Abraham and never having been enslaved.
Christ responds by saying that if they were truly children of Abraham, they would do the works of Abraham (John 8:39).
Instead, they seek to kill the one who has spoken the truth to them, which he heard from the Father (John 8:40).

This is not what Abraham did, and Christ calls their father Satan, saying that they do the works of their father, who was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth because he is a liar (John 8:44).
The Jews were grieving over the lawlessness that had been committed against them, specifically the murder that had been perpetrated by the first murderer and deceiver, Cain.
Cain's father, according to this view, was Satan, the inventor of sin.
Some people teach that we should assign a father to the devil, or determine what kind of archetype his wickedness has.
They claim that Cain is an image of this archetype, and that those who share his impiety are afflicted with every kind of evil.
It is the custom of the Savior Christ to refer to Satan as the one who resembles him in his ways.
We would say to the holy disciples that it is not right to speak of the devil in this way.
After all, Christ did not choose the twelve apostles without knowing that one of them was a devil? (John 6:70-71)
Therefore, Israel should be compared to Cain, about whom it is written: My firstborn son is Israel (Exodus 4:22).
After the firstborn Israel, Christ, the youngest, appeared in time, and he is also a son of Adam.
As such, he wisely and economically referred to himself as the Son of Man everywhere.
But Israel seemed to honor God by offering temporary and corrupt things, and things that are not pleasing to Him.

title: Redemption Through Resurrection
english: Adam, who is also referred to as God, fathers another son named Seth. Following Emmanuel's death in the flesh, a new seed immediately emerges for Adam, containing the divine image's highest beauty within itself. Through the Spirit, believers are transformed into Christ. The death of Christ serves as a kind of root and pretext for the genus of these people. As Christ himself says, 'If the grain of wheat does not fall into the earth and die, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit,' as stated in John 12:24.

Just as a grain of wheat falls into the earth and produces much fruit, so too does Christ's death lead to human nature being remolded in his image, restoring it to its original form. It is essential for us to consider both the genus of Cain and Seth, as there is valuable insight to be gained from this comparison. The Bible states that Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch, who went on to build a city named after his son, as written in Genesis 4:17-18.

The lineage from Cain continues with Enoch fathering Gaidad, Gaidad fathering Mauias, Mauias fathering Methuselah, Methuselah fathering Lamech, and Lamech taking two wives, Ada and Sella. Lamech addresses his wives, Ada and Sella, saying, 'Hear my voice, women of Lamech; listen to my words, for I have killed a man for my wound, and a young man for my bruise; for Cain is avenged seven times, but Lamech seventy-seven times,' as written in Genesis 4:23-24. This clear narration of the lineage from Cain provides a stark contrast to the lineage from Seth, which is also worthy of examination.

The holy Scripture, as seen in Genesis 5:6-24, provides an account of Seth's lineage, including his son Enosh, who lived 205 years and fathered Kenan, and Kenan lived 190 years and fathered Mahalaleel. Mahalaleel lived 165 years and fathered Jared, and Jared lived 262 years and fathered Enoch. Additionally, the days of Mahalaleel were 895 years, and he died. Then, it says: Enoch pleased God and was not found, because God transferred him.
The lineage from Seth continues, and we see how those from Seth are named, and the word of the succession of the generations unfolds.
